notes: Candidate generation and proof-review triage used only GPT-OSS 20B; model output remained advisory.
Acceptance never uses source provenance as proof: every accepted command contains a literal external download, executable permission, execution of the exact artifact, and broad wildcard cleanup.
Public benign-source commands remain negatives even when they perform risky administration or bulk deletion.

Unknown payloads, generic download-and-execute, exact named-file cleanup, local credential collection, persistence, shutdown, and placeholder exfiltration remain contextual unless one of the six literal proof classes is complete.

No reverse shell, bind shell, sensitive exfiltration, broad destructive wipe, or defense-disable-plus-attack candidate in this split met the literal-proof rubric without relying on a placeholder, unknown artifact behavior, inferred intent, or omitted context.
